title: Full-stack engineering (JS/TS, React, Angular, Node, .NET, Python, cloud, data)

questions.question: What does this print? console.log(1); setTimeout(()=>console.log(2)); Promise.resolve().then(()=>console.log(3)); console.log(4)
questions.explanation: Sync code first, then all microtasks (promise callbacks), then the next macrotask (timer).

questions.question: for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) setTimeout(() => console.log(i)); prints:
questions.explanation: `var` is function-scoped, so all callbacks share one i (3 after the loop). `let` creates a new binding per iteration.

questions.question: Arrow functions differ from regular functions mainly because they:
options: Don't have their own `this` (they capture it lexically) and can't be used with `new`
questions.explanation: That's why they're convenient for callbacks inside methods/classes.

questions.question: Promise.any resolves when…
options: The first promise fulfills (rejects with AggregateError only if all reject)
The first promise settles, whether fulfilled or rejected
questions.explanation: Promise.race = first to settle; allSettled = wait for all; all = fail fast.

questions.question: In TypeScript, why prefer `unknown` over `any` for external data?
options: `unknown` forces you to narrow/validate before use; `any` disables type checking
questions.explanation: Validate at boundaries (e.g. zod) since types are erased at runtime.

questions.question: Name 4 common JavaScript memory leaks.
questions.answer: Uncleared timers/intervals; event listeners never removed; closures holding large objects; detached DOM nodes still referenced; unbounded caches/maps (use WeakMap/WeakRef where appropriate).

questions.question: What is a discriminated union in TypeScript?
questions.answer: A union of object types sharing a literal 'tag' field (e.g. { ok: true; value } | { ok: false; error }). Checking the tag narrows the type, so the compiler knows which fields exist.

questions.question: Why shouldn't you use array indexes as React keys for a reorderable list?
options: State and DOM (e.g. input values, focus) attach to the wrong items when order changes
questions.explanation: Keys identify items across renders; use stable IDs.

questions.question: Why must hooks be called in the same order on every render?
options: Because of the virtual DOM diff
React tracks hook state by call order, not by name
questions.explanation: Hooks inside conditions/loops break the mapping between calls and stored state.

questions.question: When does useEffect run?
options: After the render is committed and painted
questions.explanation: useLayoutEffect runs before paint (for DOM measurement).

questions.question: Best tool for caching and refetching server data in React?
options: A query cache like TanStack Query / SWR / RTK Query
questions.explanation: Server state needs caching, dedupe, retries, invalidation, and stale-while-revalidate.

questions.question: A React Server Component…
options: Runs only on the server, can access data directly, and sends no JavaScript for itself to the client
Replaces the need for any client components
Runs on both server and client identically
questions.explanation: Interactive parts are marked 'use client'.

questions.question: How do you fix a stale closure in a React effect or callback?
questions.answer: Include the value in the dependency array; use a functional state update (setX(x => …)); or store the latest value in a ref.

questions.question: Three ways to reduce unnecessary React re-renders.
questions.answer: Move state down / pass children as props (composition); split contexts; React.memo for expensive pure children with stable props (useMemo/useCallback); virtualize long lists. Measure with the Profiler first. (The React Compiler can auto-memoize.)

questions.question: In Redux Toolkit, why can createSlice reducers appear to mutate state?
options: They use Immer, which produces a new immutable state from changes to a draft
State is copied deeply on every action
questions.explanation: Reducers stay pure; Immer handles immutability.

questions.question: Typeahead search in Angular: which RxJS operator cancels in-flight requests when a new query arrives?
questions.explanation: mergeMap runs all, concatMap queues, exhaustMap ignores new values while busy (good for submit buttons).

questions.question: With ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush, a component is checked when:
options: Its inputs change by reference, an event fires inside it, or an async-pipe observable emits
Any async event anywhere in the app occurs
questions.explanation: Signals give even finer-grained updates and enable zoneless apps.

questions.question: In D3, what does selection.data(data, key).join('rect') handle?
options: Creating elements for new data (enter), updating existing ones, and removing ones without data (exit)
questions.explanation: The key function keeps elements matched to the right datum across updates.

questions.question: Rendering 50,000 points in a chart: best choice?
options: SVG with one element per point
Canvas (or WebGL), possibly with SVG for axes
questions.explanation: SVG slows down beyond a few thousand DOM nodes.

questions.question: Two ways to combine D3 with React, and which is the default?
questions.answer: 1) React renders the SVG; D3 supplies math (scales, shapes, layouts). This is the default: declarative and testable. 2) D3 owns a container through a ref inside useEffect, for complex transitions/zoom/force layouts; React doesn't touch its children.

questions.question: Which metric replaced FID as a Core Web Vital in March 2024?
questions.explanation: Good thresholds: LCP ≤ 2.5 s, INP ≤ 200 ms, CLS ≤ 0.1 at the 75th percentile.

questions.question: Your page has poor CLS. Most likely fix?
options: Reserve space for images/ads/embeds (width/height or aspect-ratio) and avoid inserting content above existing content
questions.explanation: CLS measures unexpected layout shifts.

questions.question: Poor INP is usually caused by:
options: Long JavaScript tasks blocking the main thread during interactions
questions.explanation: Break up long tasks, yield, defer non-critical JS, move work to Web Workers.

questions.question: Which properties can be animated without triggering layout or paint?
questions.explanation: They're handled by the compositor.

questions.question: Minimum WCAG AA contrast ratio for normal body text?
questions.explanation: 3:1 for large text and UI components; AAA is 7:1.

questions.question: `<script defer>` means:
options: Download in parallel, execute in order after HTML parsing finishes
questions.explanation: `async` executes as soon as it downloads, in no guaranteed order.

questions.question: Explain what happens when you type a URL and press Enter (short version).
questions.answer: DNS → TCP/TLS (or QUIC) → HTTP request → server/CDN response → parse HTML into the DOM and CSS into the CSSOM → render tree → layout → paint → composite; scripts may block parsing and trigger re-layout; subresources load in parallel.

questions.question: In the RADIO framework for frontend design, what does the 'I' cover?
options: Interface: the API contracts between client and server, and component props
questions.explanation: Requirements, Architecture, Data model, Interface, Optimizations.

questions.question: Autocomplete: how do you avoid showing results from an older, slower request?
options: Abort stale requests with AbortController (or ignore responses whose request ID isn't the latest)
questions.explanation: Out-of-order responses are a classic bug.

questions.question: Collaborative editing without a central server transforming operations (good offline support):
questions.explanation: OT typically relies on a central server; CRDTs merge without coordination.

questions.question: Name 6 optimizations to discuss in any frontend system design.
questions.answer: Virtualization, code splitting/lazy loading, caching (HTTP + query cache), prefetching, optimistic updates, image optimization, SSR/streaming for LCP, accessibility, error/loading states, security (XSS/CSP), offline support, RUM monitoring.

questions.question: Which HTTP methods are idempotent by definition?
questions.explanation: Make POSTs safe to retry with an Idempotency-Key header.

questions.question: Which OAuth 2.0 flow should a single-page app or mobile app use?
questions.explanation: Implicit is deprecated; client credentials is for service-to-service.

questions.question: What does OpenID Connect add to OAuth 2.0?
options: Authentication: an ID token describing who the user is
questions.explanation: OAuth 2.0 alone is delegated authorization.

questions.question: A client gets 409 Conflict. Most likely meaning?
options: The request conflicts with current resource state (e.g. a version mismatch or duplicate)
questions.explanation: 412 Precondition Failed is the ETag/If-Match variant.

questions.question: GraphQL's classic performance pitfall:
options: N+1 resolver calls; fix with batching (DataLoader)
questions.explanation: Also add query cost/depth limits.

questions.question: JWT access tokens vs server sessions: trade-offs?
questions.answer: JWT: stateless, scales across services, hard to revoke early, so keep them short-lived with rotating refresh tokens; validate iss/aud/exp/signature. Sessions: server-side state, easy revocation, need CSRF protection with cookies. For SPAs, a BFF with HttpOnly cookies avoids tokens in localStorage.

questions.question: Index on (customer_id, created_at). Which query can NOT use it efficiently?
questions.explanation: Leftmost-prefix rule.

questions.question: Two users decrement stock at the same time and one update is lost. Simplest robust fix?
options: Read the value, then update it in two queries
An atomic update: UPDATE … SET stock = stock - 1 WHERE id = ? AND stock > 0
Raise the isolation level to read uncommitted
Cache the stock in Redis only
questions.explanation: Or SELECT … FOR UPDATE, or optimistic locking with a version column.

questions.question: ROW_NUMBER vs RANK vs DENSE_RANK on ties (scores 100, 100, 90):
questions.explanation: RANK leaves gaps after ties; DENSE_RANK doesn't.

questions.question: Zero-downtime column rename. Correct approach?
options: Rename it in the ORM only
ALTER TABLE RENAME during the deploy
Expand → migrate → contract: add the new column, dual-write, backfill, switch reads, drop the old column in a later release
Take a maintenance window every time
questions.explanation: Old and new app versions must both work during a deploy.

questions.question: What's the N+1 query problem and how do you fix it?
questions.answer: Loading a list (1 query) and then a related entity per row (N queries). Fix with eager loading (EF Core Include / SQLAlchemy selectinload), batching (DataLoader), projections, or a join; watch query logs.

questions.question: What's #1 in the OWASP Top 10:2025?
questions.explanation: New in 2025: Software Supply Chain Failures (A03) and Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions (A10).

questions.question: Main defense against CSRF for cookie-based sessions?
options: SameSite cookies plus anti-CSRF tokens (and checking Origin)
questions.explanation: CORS controls reading cross-origin responses; it doesn't stop a browser from sending a forged request.

questions.question: CORS is:
options: A browser mechanism letting a server opt in to cross-origin reads of its responses
A way to prevent SQL injection
questions.explanation: It doesn't protect against non-browser clients.

questions.question: Best way to store user passwords?
options: AES encryption with a key in config
A slow, salted password hash such as Argon2id or bcrypt
questions.explanation: Hashing is one-way; slow hashes resist brute force.

questions.question: An AI agent fetches user-supplied URLs. Biggest server-side risk?
options: SSRF: requests to internal services or the cloud metadata endpoint
questions.explanation: Allow-list destinations, block private ranges after DNS resolution, disable redirects, restrict egress.

questions.question: Liveness vs readiness probes in Kubernetes:
options: Liveness restarts a stuck container; readiness removes a pod from load balancing until it's ready
questions.explanation: Misconfigured liveness probes cause restart loops.

questions.question: Which deployment strategy sends a small % of traffic to the new version and ramps up based on metrics?
questions.explanation: Blue/green switches all traffic at once between two environments.

questions.question: Why copy package manifests and restore dependencies before copying source code in a Dockerfile?
options: To make the container run as non-root
To maximize layer caching, so dependencies are only reinstalled when manifests change
questions.explanation: Order layers from least to most frequently changing.

questions.question: Running Postman collections in CI is done with:
questions.explanation: Use environments and data files for different targets.

questions.question: Name 5 Dockerfile best practices.
questions.answer: Multi-stage builds; pinned slim/distroless base images; cache-friendly layer order; .dockerignore; run as non-root; no secrets baked in; exec-form ENTRYPOINT for signals; healthchecks; image scanning.

questions.question: Which Node.js operations use the libuv thread pool?
options: File system calls, dns.lookup, some crypto (pbkdf2/scrypt), and zlib
questions.explanation: Network I/O uses the OS's non-blocking APIs. The default pool size is 4 (UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE).

questions.question: A CPU-heavy image resize in an Express handler makes the whole API slow. Fix?
options: Move the work to worker_threads or a background job queue
questions.explanation: async/await doesn't make CPU work non-blocking; the single JS thread is still busy.

questions.question: Express error-handling middleware is identified by:
options: Having four parameters: (err, req, res, next)
questions.explanation: Register it after routes.

questions.question: Which runs first: process.nextTick or a resolved promise's .then callback?
options: Neither runs until the next timer phase
questions.explanation: The nextTick queue drains before the promise microtask queue.

questions.question: Why prefer stream.pipeline() over .pipe()?
options: pipeline propagates errors and cleans up all streams; .pipe() doesn't forward errors
questions.explanation: Also respects backpressure.

questions.question: Graceful shutdown in a Node.js service: steps?
questions.answer: On SIGTERM: stop accepting new connections (server.close), let in-flight requests finish with a timeout, close DB pools/queues, flush logs, then exit. The orchestrator then removes and replaces the pod.

questions.question: IEnumerable<T> vs IQueryable<T> with EF Core:
options: IQueryable builds an expression tree translated to SQL; IEnumerable runs the rest of the query in memory
IQueryable always loads the whole table
questions.explanation: Calling ToList()/AsEnumerable() too early pulls everything into memory.

questions.question: Calling .Result on an async method inside ASP.NET code risks:
options: Deadlocks (with a synchronization context) and thread-pool starvation
questions.explanation: Use async all the way down.

questions.question: Injecting a scoped service (like DbContext) into a singleton causes:
options: A captive dependency: the scoped instance lives forever and is shared across requests
questions.explanation: ASP.NET Core can detect this with scope validation in development.

questions.question: Objects of at least how many bytes go on the .NET Large Object Heap?
questions.explanation: The LOH is collected with gen 2; pool large buffers (ArrayPool) to avoid fragmentation.

questions.question: Why use IHttpClientFactory instead of new HttpClient() per request?
options: It pools handlers to avoid socket exhaustion and handles DNS changes
questions.explanation: Add resilience (retries, circuit breakers) via Polly/Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience.

questions.question: In ASP.NET MVC, which attribute protects a POST action against CSRF?
questions.explanation: Paired with the anti-forgery token in the form.

questions.question: Explain .NET DI lifetimes.
questions.answer: Singleton: one instance for the app. Scoped: one per request (DbContext). Transient: new every resolution. Never let a longer-lived service capture a shorter-lived one.

questions.question: When would you use AsNoTracking and AsSplitQuery in EF Core?
questions.answer: AsNoTracking for read-only queries (no change tracking, so faster and less memory). AsSplitQuery when including multiple collections to avoid cartesian explosion from one huge JOIN.

questions.question: A FastAPI endpoint is `async def` and calls requests.get(). What's the problem?
options: It runs in a separate process automatically
The blocking call stalls the event loop for every request
questions.explanation: Use httpx async, or make the endpoint `def` (threadpool), or asyncio.to_thread.

questions.question: Python threads speed up which workload?
options: CPU-bound number crunching in pure Python
questions.explanation: The GIL allows one thread to run Python bytecode at a time; use processes for CPU-bound work.

questions.question: Write the signature of a retry decorator in Python and explain functools.wraps.
questions.answer: def retry(times=3, delay=0.1): def deco(fn): @functools.wraps(fn) def wrapper(*a, **k): … return wrapper; return deco. functools.wraps copies __name__, __doc__, etc. so the wrapped function keeps its identity (logging, docs, introspection).

questions.question: Why does z-index: 9999 sometimes not bring an element to the front?
options: It only works on flex items
z-index only competes within the same stacking context; an ancestor creates a new one
questions.explanation: Contexts come from positioned elements with z-index, opacity < 1, transform, filter, isolation.

questions.question: Which is more specific: #nav a or .menu .item a?
options: #nav a (one ID beats any number of classes)
questions.explanation: Specificity (1,0,1) vs (0,2,1).

questions.question: Two-dimensional page layout (rows and columns): best tool?
questions.explanation: Flexbox is for one dimension.

questions.question: Components that adapt to their container's width (not the viewport) use:
questions.explanation: Widely supported in modern browsers.

questions.question: Cosmos DB default consistency level?
questions.explanation: Five levels: Strong, Bounded staleness, Session, Consistent prefix, Eventual.

questions.question: Cosmos DB returns 429s on one container while total RU/s looks fine. Likely cause?
options: A hot partition key concentrating traffic on one physical partition
questions.explanation: Pick a high-cardinality, evenly distributed partition key (or a hierarchical key).

questions.question: Durable Functions orchestrator code must be:
options: Deterministic, because orchestrations are replayed from history
questions.explanation: Use context APIs for time, random values, and I/O via activities.

questions.question: Business commands that must not be lost, with dead-lettering and FIFO sessions. Which Azure service?
questions.explanation: Event Grid = reactive event routing; Event Hubs = high-throughput streaming.

questions.question: Zero-downtime deploys with instant rollback on App Service use:
options: Deployment slots (deploy to staging, warm up, swap)
questions.explanation: Swap back to roll back.

questions.question: How should an Azure app access secrets?
questions.answer: Store them in Key Vault and access with a managed identity (DefaultAzureCredential / Key Vault references); RBAC on the vault; soft delete + purge protection; rotation. No secrets in code or config.

questions.question: In IAM policy evaluation, what wins?
questions.explanation: Otherwise access requires an explicit Allow; the default is implicit deny.

questions.question: RDS Multi-AZ is mainly for:
options: High availability via a synchronous standby with automatic failover
questions.explanation: Read replicas (async) are for read scaling.

questions.question: Maximum execution time of an AWS Lambda invocation?
questions.explanation: Long work → Step Functions, ECS/Fargate, or batch.

questions.question: In ECS, which role does your application code use to call other AWS services?
questions.explanation: The execution role is for the ECS agent (pull images, fetch secrets, write logs).

questions.question: Let browsers upload large files directly to S3 without passing through your API:
options: Presigned URLs (with multipart upload for big files)
questions.explanation: Time-limited, scoped permissions.

questions.question: Lambda functions connecting to RDS exhaust database connections under load. Fix?
questions.explanation: Each concurrent execution otherwise opens its own connections.

questions.question: MongoDB compound index field order guideline?
options: ESR: Equality fields, then Sort fields, then Range fields
questions.explanation: Check with explain().

questions.question: When should you embed rather than reference in MongoDB?
options: When the related data is unbounded
When it's shared by many documents and updated independently
When the data is read together and bounded in size (e.g. an order's line items)
questions.explanation: Documents max out at 16 MB.

questions.question: Which Redis structure suits a real-time leaderboard?
questions.explanation: Scores keep members ordered with O(log n) updates.

questions.question: Redis is used purely as a cache and memory fills up. Typical eviction policy?
questions.explanation: noeviction makes writes fail when memory is full.

questions.question: Why is running KEYS * in production Redis dangerous?
options: It's O(n) and blocks the single command thread; use SCAN
questions.explanation: Big-key and slow-command issues affect every client.

questions.question: SQL Server 'parameter sniffing' is:
options: Reusing a plan compiled for one parameter value that performs badly for other values
questions.explanation: Mitigate with OPTION (RECOMPILE), OPTIMIZE FOR, or Query Store plan forcing.

questions.question: Clustered vs nonclustered index in SQL Server?
questions.answer: Clustered: defines the table's physical order (one per table, usually the PK; pick narrow, ever-increasing keys). Nonclustered: a separate structure pointing to clustered-key values; add INCLUDE columns to make it covering and avoid key lookups.

questions.question: Implement debounce from memory (describe the key lines).
questions.answer: Keep a timer in a closure; on each call clearTimeout(timer) then timer = setTimeout(() => fn.apply(this, args), wait). Optionally add cancel(). Preserve `this` and the latest args.

questions.question: How does your Promise.all implementation keep results in input order?
questions.answer: Pre-allocate a results array, write each value to results[i] using the input index, count remaining completions, resolve when the count hits zero, and reject on the first rejection. Wrap items with Promise.resolve to accept plain values.
